Then Roupen, when he was delivered,
went back and took those places;
and the Prince began to ravage the whole country of Cilicia with plundering.
And at that time Pahlawan, the ruler of Persia, was killed,
and many slaughters took place in the midst.
And also the Kurds and the Turcomans clashed with one another near Nisibis,
for the reason
that a certain Turcoman man went and took a wife from other Turcomans;
and when the wedding guests passed by one of the fortresses of the Kurds in the land of Zawzan,
the Kurds stood by their way
and demanded from them the wedding feast toll.
And when the Turcomans resisted,
the Kurds overpowered them,
and snatched the bride and went up to their fortress.
And from this a great war began,
and the roads were cut off,
and caravans were plundered,
and from both sides about ten thousand were killed.
And again the Kurds assembled, about thirty thousand,
and encountered the Turcomans near the Khabur;
and the Kurds were defeated,
and their slain fell from the banks of the river Khabur as far as Nisibis.
And again twice they encountered one another in the region of Mosul,
and the Kurds were defeated.
And again several times in Syria the Turcomans defeated the Kurds,
and pursued after them as far as Cilicia,
and killed men and women, down to infants.
And when the Turcomans had wiped out the Kurds from all Syria and Mesopotamia,
they entered Armenia,
and took twenty-six thousand of the Armenians as slaves and sold them.
And the great monastery of Garbid (or Girbid) they burned down,
and the monks they killed.
And from Telbesmi, which is in the region of Mardin,
one hundred and seventy Syrian men from among our people were killed.
And from Amron, a village in the region of Claudia in the domain of Melitene,
two hundred young men bearing arms from among our people were killed.
And in all Cappadocia and in the region of Melitene,
fierce battles and many slaughters took place.
And also the Arabs and the Ismailis encountered one another,
and many were killed.
And in that same year division fell among the Franks,
